To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
cell signalling pathways are highly dynamic and are controlled at multiple levels, including the synthesis, activation, localization, degradation and inactivation of signalling components.
The cell signalling pathways that control the development of multicellular animals are conserved and used to control a wide variety of different processes in adult cells.
the cell signalling system consists of a network of interconnected signalling modules that can be activated in a variety of different ways and can be regulated at different levels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the molecular basis of how cells communicate and co-ordinate their activities.
understanding the way cells use their signalling toolkit.
understanding the biology of cell signaling.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
cell signalling is the process by which cells communicate with each other and with their environment.
cell signalling is a complex and dynamic process.
the aim of this website, is to describe the biology of cell signaling.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a new signalling system, which we call the "p38 MAPK pathway" that is involved in cell proliferation, differentiation and apoptosis.
cell signalling is a fundamental mechanism for controlling cell function and cell behaviour.
we have developed and validated a new method for the identification of cell surface receptors and their ligands in a cell type specific manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
cell signalling is a highly integrated process, with different signalling pathways working in combination and in parallel to control specific cellular functions.
cell signalling pathways are highly adaptable, and can be combined and reconfigured to control a wide range of different biological processes in widely different cellular and developmental contexts.
cell signalling is a highly dynamic process that is constantly changing to adapt to the needs of the cell.
